messages:
anya: Heads up — hit two customer cases where requests to private endpoints with both a pool header and a token-scoped workspace ended up routed to a dedicated pool that didn't match the token scope. Example (sanitized):

anya: ```
POST /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer sk-customer
X-RW-Workspace: workspace_abc
X-RW-Pool-Id: pool_dedicated_42
```

anya: Current behavior seems to prefer X-RW-Pool-Id over token workspace. Is that by design? worried about header spoofing when gateways are misconfigured.

rob: I think the intended precedence was: explicit pool_id (if the pool is owned by the workspace) -> workspace header -> token scope -> default shared pools. but we never enforced "owned by workspace" check. that gap explains the customer hit.

samira: for console/UX: we should show the "effective routing decision" on the request inspector with a short rationale string (e.g., "chose pool_dedicated_42 because X-RW-Pool-Id matched configured pool for workspace_abc"). that'll make triage easier.

mike: security note: never trust inbound headers from external proxies unless they're authenticated. we need either to: 1) strip these headers at the edge and re-insert from a trusted ingress, OR 2) sign them. prefer 1, but for private endpoints customers sometimes terminate TLS upstream and inject headers.

mike: sketch for a signing approach (HMAC):

mike: ```
# header payload: workspace=workspace_abc;pool=pool_dedicated_42;ts=1670000000
sig = HMAC_SHA256(shared_secret, payload)
X-RW-Scope: workspace=workspace_abc;pool=pool_dedicated_42;ts=1670000000
X-RW-Scope-Sig: <base64(sig)>
```

rob: +1 to strict validation. gateway should validate pool ownership against the tenant DB and reject when mismatch. also emit a telemetry event for "routing_mismatch" that includes which source won and why (header vs token vs pool binding).

cecilia: billing/quotas question: if a request routes to a dedicated pool owned by workspace A but bearer token belongs to workspace B (malicious header spoof), which quota applies? we need to be explicit: capacity routing != billing identity. billing and per-workspace quota enforcement must be driven from the token identity only.

rob: agree. routing decides where to run, quotas/billing decide limits. gateway must reconcile: if routing target != token workspace, run with target pool but enforce token workspace quota and log an alert. do not give elevated rates/capacity to token that doesn't own the pool.

samira: for rollout UX: let's add a toggle in the console "allow pool header override" (off by default) per-org and show a caution modal explaining risks. add an audit log entry whenever an override is honored.

deploy-bot: preflight check: there's an open PR at https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/485 that adds a validation step for pool ownership and emits telemetry metric routing.mismatch.count (env: staging). CI green.

anya: action items: (1) rob: add ownership check + telemetry (2) mike: design header signing + doc + edge-stripping guidance (3) samira: console inspector + per-org toggle + audit log UX (4) infra: ensure ingress strips untrusted headers by default. i'll file tickets for each.

rob: i'll also add unit tests that simulate: token workspace != workspace header, pool exists but owned by diff workspace, unsigned header present, signed header valid.

mike: i'll draft an RFC for X-RW-Scope-Sig and a migration plan for partners. will ping @samira for the UX copy.

cecilia: add a telemetry delta for billing anomalies so finance can detect unexpected usage re-routing.

anya: perfect. assigning now. :thumbsup:
